claims.disproof_condition: Reverse this near-term-safe reading if Proterial's NMX-G1NH-HF (spec'd for 'high torque and heat resistance' per its own PR) or any competitor demonstrates H/SH-grade thermal performance in independent or OEM qualification testing — that would re-arm the HRE-demand threat at full strength.
claims.statement: Independent industry assessment (Rare Earth Exchanges, expert Aminul Mehedi) challenges the near-term EV-traction viability of Proterial's HRE-free magnets: at best M grade (~100°C) versus the H grade (120°C) minimum and SH grade (150°C) ideal that EV/wind/A&D applications require — 'more of a scientific milestone than a commercial solution' pending independent testing. Consequence for the heavy-REO axis: the HRE-free threat to Dy/Tb demand is NOT imminent at disclosed specs, which near-term SUPPORTS the Lynas/MP heavy-REO positioning while the [370] disproof watch stays armed. Also noted: Proterial's 600+ global patent filings signal the HRE-free/GBD battleground may be IP litigation — relevant to the parked GBD patent-structure question.

source_doc.title: Rare Earth Exchanges — Proterial's Heavy Rare Earth-Free Magnet Claim: Breakthrough or Litigation Trap?

sources.quote: Their heavy RE-free magnets are at best M grade, whereas EVs, wind turbine generators, and A&D applications need a bare minimum H grade (120 °C) and ideally SH grade (150 °C).
Until independent testing confirms they can match or beat the performance of today's industry-standard magnets...the breakthrough remains more of a scientific milestone than a commercial solution.
the company's patent-heavy posture—over 600 global filings, 200+ in Japan—suggests the next battlefield in rare earths may not be geology, but intellectual property litigation.
